title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page '- 16 -' of a typed draft, printed upside down relative to the scan, which appears to be a Bourbaki-style draft on analytic functions or power series in a Banach algebra. It was probably reused as scrap paper inside the 1965 'motifs' notes. The surrounding pages, on Picard categories of Breen and localisation for abelian varieties, are unrelated to it.

The page first ends a proof. E is a commutative normed (Banach) algebra over K = R or C, with constant a in the norm inequality, and u is an element with ||u|| < 1/5a. The binomial series h(u) for sqrt(e+u) converges absolutely. The identity (h(u))^2 = e + u follows from the corresponding scalar identity for sqrt(1-4x) when E = K = R; the text cites Fonctions d'une variable réelle, chap. III, §2. Uniqueness: let g and g1 be continuous with value e at 0 and with g^2 = g1^2 = f. Commutativity gives (g - g1)(g + g1) = 0. Since g + g1 equals 2e at 0, it is invertible near 0, so g = g1 locally.

It then opens '§2. La méthode des majorantes'. Definition 1: a power series in p variables with positive real coefficients C_n majorizes a power series with coefficients c_n in E if ||c_n|| <= C_n for every multi-index n. The text notes that majorants of a sum or product give a majorant of the sum or product. It also notes that if the majorant is summable at (r_1, ..., r_p), the given series is absolutely summable on the closed polydisc |z_i| <= r_i. The converse statement is begun but cut off.

This is the standard Cauchy method of majorants, written in Bourbaki's expository style.
errors: As transcribed, the formula (1 - Σ_{n≥1} binom(2n,n) x^n)^2 = 1 - 4x is false. The correct expansion is sqrt(1-4x) = 1 - Σ_{n≥1} binom(2n,n) x^n/(2n-1), with coefficients 2, 2, 4, 10, ... (twice the Catalan numbers). Either the typescript omits the factor 1/(2n-1) or the transcription does.
The bound 1/5a is not sharp: the radius for the scalar series is 1/4, so 1/(4a) would suffice. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Square root of e+u in a commutative Banach algebra via the binomial series, with local uniqueness among continuous functions equal to e at the origin
ideas.modern_name: Holomorphic functional calculus / binomial series in Banach algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gelfand school; Bourbaki, Théories spectrales / Variétés différentielles et analytiques)

ideas.what: Majorant series for power series in several variables with coefficients in a normed space; stability under sum and product; absolute convergence on polydiscs
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy's method of majorants (calcul des limites)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats (and drafts)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused typed page of a standard Bourbaki-style exposition on power series and majorants. It has no connection to the motivic or Picard-category content of the surrounding notes and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down; the text is a typescript ('- 16 -'), not Grothendieck's handwriting.

The closing words '(1 ≤ i ≤ p). Inversement, supposons qu'une série entière ... soit absolument sommable dans le polycylindre fermé' are correctly read; the sentence continues on the next typed page, which is not present.
